- Overestimate in early periods after sharp price spikes; reduce forecast by 5–10% for the next 3–5 days post-spike.
- Underestimate when historical mean is low (e.g., <65) and recent prices are trending down; adjust upward by 2–5% for 3–7 day horizon.
- Overshoot in mid-term forecasts (e.g., 10–20 day horizon) when historical volatility is high; apply a 3–5% downward correction.
- Lagging bias: if model is 2–3 days ahead of true price, reduce forecast by 1–2% per day lag.
- Mean reversion bias: if forecast is >10% above 30-day moving average, reduce by 1–3% per day until convergence.
- Avoid overconfidence in short-term spikes; cap forecast at 10% above recent 7-day high unless confirmed by volume or policy signals.
